About / Brand Story content:
AVZ Vaganza started the way a lot of good things do: staring at a stuffed closet, completely sick of seeing the exact same fast fashion clones on every single person on the street. Tired of the endless cycle of waste and clothes heading straight to landfills, the founder grabbed a pair of scissors and started cutting up her own clothes to build something entirely different.
That mindset built the brand. AVZ Vaganza doesn't care about mass production or churning out endless inventory. There is no factory mindset here, just an obsession with craftsmanship, raw materials, and keeping things intentional.
In a world drowning in fast fashion and AI-generated sameness, real, messy, human hands making things is the ultimate luxury. Because at the end of the day, we aren't just selling clothes or accessories. We’re selling art.
Founder / designer biography:
Known to the world as Dhrisni or Dhristroyer, she wears many titles like model, actor, content creator, and designer. But if you strip all of that away, at her absolute core, she is just an artist. She has spent most of her life making art, long before any brand or platform came into the picture. Growing up in a household where she was not allowed to wear revealing clothes, not even sleeveless tops, her creativity had to find some kind of outlet. That restriction is what first pushed her to pick up a pair of scissors and start cutting up clothes for Instagram.
As her life shifted and she grew as a creator, she found herself surrounded by clothes that all looked painfully simple. She hates simple. She despises minimalism, loathes cookie cutter aesthetics, and has zero patience for AI generated sameness. She is all about maximalism, chaos, texture, and raw human grit.
Her two hands are literally her favorite things about her body because they are the tools that turn junk, hardware, and scraps into something breathing and alive. In a world rushing toward digital convenience and fast fashion factories, building things with her own two hands is the ultimate rebellion. She does not care about mass quantities, she only cares about the craft. Through her work, she wants people to love art, to deeply appreciate and respect the labor behind it, and to help keep real, tangible creativity alive. Because she is not just making clothes. She is making art, and it is here to take up space.

Frequently Asked Questions: About AVZ Vaganza (Aveezah Vaganza) & The Creator
Q: What is AVZ Vaganza (Aveezah Vaganza) and who is behind it?
A: AVZ Vaganza (Aveezah Vaganza) is an independent, sustainable, and alternative high fashion label founded, directed, and designed by Dhrisni, also known online as Dhristroyer. Dhrisni is an artist first who also works across modeling, acting, and digital creation, and she pours her entire creative soul into building wearable art rather than factory made fast fashion.
Q: Where did the brand start?
A: It started out of pure rebellion. Growing up in a household where strict clothing rules meant no revealing outfits or even sleeveless tops, Dhrisni had to find an outlet for her creativity. She grabbed a pair of scissors, started cutting up her own clothes for Instagram, and never looked back.
Q: What is the design philosophy of AVZ Vaganza (Aveezah Vaganza)?
A: Absolute maximalism, texture, chaos, and grit. The brand fiercely rejects minimalism, cookie cutter aesthetics, and AI generated sameness. It specializes in subcultural styles like cyber grunge, Y2K, mermaidcore, industrial punk, and avant garde streetwear, built from non traditional materials like computer motherboards, mechanical keyboard keycaps, chainmail, metal spikes, and upcycled hardware.
Q: Are the pieces mass produced?
A: Never. AVZ Vaganza (Aveezah Vaganza) does not care about mass quantities or factory lines because the focus is entirely on craftsmanship, raw materials, and keeping true, tangible art alive. The brand exclusively hires and trains women directly under Dhrisni's supervision to handcraft the pieces. In a world drowning in fast fashion and digital convenience, things made by real human hands are the ultimate luxury.
